(Through Video Conferencing) Dt:21.07.2020 Seeking quashment of proceedings in C.C.No.412 of 2019 on the file of the I Additional Junior Civil Judge, Sattenapalli, Guntur District, registered against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 273, 420, 120-B IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the Act"), the present criminal petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1972.

entities.text: I Additional Junior Civil Judge, Sattenapalli, Guntur District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance on the common order dated 18.12.2019 passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, holding that "tobacco" does not fall within the definition of "food", as specified under Section 3(i)(j) of the Act,
therefore, registration of crime is not permissible .
Reliance has also been placed on the common order dated 05.03.2020 passed by another coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5103 of 2019 and batch, quashing the FIRs., therein.
In view of the aforesaid, it is urged that the crime may be quashed.

On the other hand, though the Public Prosecutor opposed the relief prayed for, but, he is not in a position to dispute the fact that various petitions filed before this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
have been allowed and FIRs., have been quashed on the basis of the analogy has put forth by the Boorlagadda Nageswara Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 21 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36494824/
1 petitioner before this Court.
Considering the aforesaid and looking to the undisputed fact that, previously, FIRs., have been quashed by this Court in similar matters, however, proceeding with trial in the present case is wholly undesirable.

sentences.text: So far as the allegation regarding Section 420 IPC is concerned, it is to be observed that the offence has been registered on account of seizure of Tobacco, treating it within the purview of "food" and thus the said offence has been quashed hereinabove; however, looking to the allegation, the ingredients of Section 420 IPC do not subsist.

In that view of the matter, this Criminal Petition is allowed and proceedings in C.C.No.412 of 2019 on the file of the I Additional Junior Civil Judge, Sattenapalli, Guntur District, are hereby quashed

Counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance on the common order dated 18.12.2019 passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, holding that "tobacco" does not fall within the definition of "food", as specified under Section 3(i)(j) of the Act,
therefore, registration of crime is not permissible .

Reliance has also been placed on the common order dated 05.03.2020 passed by another coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5103 of 2019 and batch, quashing the FIRs., therein.

1 petitioner before this Court.
Considering the aforesaid and looking to the undisputed fact that, previously, FIRs., have been quashed by this Court in similar matters, however, proceeding with trial in the present case is wholly undesirable.
